candidates.exact_span: a. Reporting periods shall end on the last day of each month.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The calendar boundary for reporting periods can change how reported values are grouped into monthly averages and which monitoring-period obligations apply when evaluating measurements against limits.

candidates.exact_span:
3. If any 30 day average, monthly average, 7 day average, weekly average, or daily maximum
   value exceeds the effluent limitations specified in Part I.A, the permittee shall report the
   excursion in accordance with the requirements of Part III.D.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This clause enumerates the averaging bases and maximum types that trigger excursion reporting against Part I.A limits; interpreting which average type applies to a reported measurement changes both the applicable limit comparison (A) and whether excursion reporting was required (B).

candidates.exact_span:
4. Any 30 day average, monthly average, 7 day average, weekly average, or daily maximum
   value reported in the required Discharge Monitoring Report which is in excess of the effluent
   limitation specified in Part I.A shall constitute evidence of violation of such effluent
   limitation and of this permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The linkage between specific reported average/maximum types and Part I.A effluent limitations affects which reported values are treated as exceeding an enforceable numeric limit versus report-only data not subject to numeric compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span:
5. Other measurements of oxygen demand (e.g., TOC and COD) may be substituted for five
   day Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD5) or for five day Carbonaceous Biochemical
   Oxygen Demand (CBOD5), as applicable, where the permittee can demonstrate long term
   correlation of the method with BOD5 or CBOD5 values, as applicable. Details of the
   correlation procedures used must be submitted and prior approval granted by the permitting
   authority for this procedure to be acceptable. Data reported must also include evidence to
   show that the proper correlation continues to exist after approval.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether TOC or COD may stand in for BOD5/CBOD5—and whether correlation and prior approval are satisfied—changes which numeric limit applies to reported oxygen-demand measurements (A) and how missing or alternate-parameter results are classified when BOD5/CBOD5 data are absent (C).

candidates.exact_span:
The permittee shall report all overflows with the Discharge Monitoring Report submittal. These
reports shall be summarized and reported in tabular format. The summaries shall include: the
date, time, duration, location, estimated volume, and cause of the overflow; observed
environmental impacts from the overflow; actions taken to address the overflow; and ultimate
discharge location if not contained (e.g., storm sewer system, ditch, tributary).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Overflow reporting is a discharge-dependent monitoring obligation; whether overflows occurred and were documented affects established monitoring requirements (B) and whether periods without ordinary numeric results reflect documented discharge events versus other no-data states (C).
